title: I built an AI-narrated RPG where the engine, not the model, rolls the dice. Here's how it works (and I'm looking for testers)
author: MacSnig
selftext:
I've spent the last few months building Kith Moot, a fantasy RPG on the fifth edition SRD with an LLM as the narrator. The main thing I wanted to fix from other AI story games: the model inventing outcomes, handing out gold you never found, or forgetting your HP.



\*\*How it works:\*\*



\- The narrator never writes game state. It can only propose what happens, and a rules engine checks every proposal against the SRD and the character sheet before anything changes.

\- The engine rolls the dice before the narrator writes, so the story has to fit the roll, not the other way round.

\- If the narrator describes something the engine didn't allow, the reply gets rewritten.

\- The portraits and backdrops were painted locally with an image model on a MacBook Air.



\*\*What's hardest:\*\* narrator drift. Getting a model to describe only what actually happened, every time, is a much harder problem than I expected, and it's where most of my time goes.



\*\*Who it's for:\*\* people who like tabletop-style fantasy, solo or with a small group, and don't want to fuss with a DM or an engine that can cheat or forget your gear.



It's in closed beta now. If you'd like to try it and pick it apart (or make suggestions), request an invite at https://kithmoot.com/beta/. It's free during the closed beta, and closed beta testers get founder pricing through open beta and launch.



Happy to answer questions.
